methodological_rigor.justification: Retrospective single-center study (n=28 R/R DLBCL with glofitamab), stratified by LAG3 rs870849 SNPs. Severe imbalance: I455hom subgroup n=6 (83% male, 33% prior CAR-T); T455hom n=11 (36% male, 91% prior CAR-T). Small subgroups with wide CI on estimates (HR 14-16 for PFS/OS). No correction for multiple testing despite examining two genes. Univariate and multivariable Cox regression with limited power. Imbalances not adequately controlled despite multivariable adjustment.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Small retrospective case series (n=28) in highly selected multi-drug resistant R/R DLBCL, mostly CAR-T refractory. Clinical relevance speculative; LAG3 association may be prognostic in this extreme population but not generalizable to broader R/R DLBCL. LoE 4 (small case series).

reporting_quality.justification: Methods described for genetic analysis and statistical testing. However, limited detail on DNA extraction quality control, no data sharing mentioned, no code availability. Baseline characteristics show extreme imbalance but limited discussion of its impact.

novelty_literature.justification: LAG3 polymorphisms in treatment response previously studied in CAR-T context. Current application to glofitamab is incremental extension with identical SNP and similar methodology.

writing_presentation.justification: Organized presentation with Kaplan-Meier curves showing LAG3 dose-dependent effect. Discussion appropriately acknowledges limitations (small sample, selection bias, imbalance in baseline characteristics, overfitting risk). However, presentation leads with dramatic HR estimates without adequate emphasis on instability.

key_strengths: First study of LAG3/CTLA4 polymorphisms in glofitamab-treated DLBCL
Clear dose-dependent LAG3 effect on survival outcomes
key_concerns: Extremely small sample (n=28) with severe baseline imbalance (sex 36-83%, prior CAR-T 33-91% across groups)
Unequal subgroup sizes (n=6-11) with extreme HR estimates (14-16) and wide CIs indicate severe instability/overfitting
Study population heavily selected (75% CAR-T refractory, multi-drug resistant); not generalizable to broader R/R DLBCL
No independent validation; results exploratory at best
Imbalances inadequately controlled despite multivariable modeling; confounding remains likely
chief_reviewer.rationale: Highly exploratory pilot in extremely small, severely imbalanced, ultra-selected population. Dramatic HR estimates with wide CIs reflect instability not robust association. Rejection at tier 4 appropriate unless authors substantially revise to emphasize extreme preclinical nature and remove or contextualize HR presentations.
